title: Bahrain
capsule: In the late eighteenth century the Bahrain archipelago in the Persian Gulf passed from Iranian to Arab control: after Nader Shah's Afsharid conquest of 1737 the islands remained under nominal Persian rule, contested by Bani Utbah tribesmen raiding from Zubarah on the Qatari coast. In 1783 the Al-Khalifa, a Bani Utbah clan, decisively defeated the Persian garrison and seized Bahrain under Ahmad bin Muhammad 'al-Fatih' ('the Conqueror'), founding the dynasty that still rules. Through the early nineteenth century the Al-Khalifa governed a pearling and entrepot economy while fending off Omani, Wahhabi, and Persian claims, and in 1820 their sheikh signed the General Treaty of Peace with Britain that began Bahrain's drift into the British Gulf protective system.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The archipelago's defined insular boundaries are well established; the attestation window 1757–1846 captures the early Al-Khalifa period before full British protectorate formalization.
